newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: World Bank sees Colombia returning to growth soon.
newsitem.headline: World Bank sees Colombia returning to growth soon.

text.p: Colombia should return to growth soon after plunging into recession for the first time in decades, the World Bank's chief Latin American economist Guillermo Perry said.

"I'm sure that at some time this year the recovery will set in, or early next year. There is no good reason why it should not," Perry told Reuters in a telephone interview from Cartagena, where he was hosting a World Bank conference.
Colombian gross domestic product fell 1.22 percent in the first quarter, in part due to an exceptionally poor 1996/7 coffee harvest. The drop was the second consecutive quarterly fall.

Government officials have said 3.5 percent growth for the year is still possible and have forecast the economy will bounce back in the second half -- led by oil and coffee and helped by low interest rates.
